lastText: The Night EndsThe Court FallsNew Ending Discovered · 1 / 15A HOUSE LIT FROM CELLAR TO ROOF, AND THEN DARKThey come at noon, and the house has been lit from cellar to roof for a week. The servants stand in the hall in a row. A great many of them are weeping, and none of them runs. You are in the chapel, in the box, with a little of your strength. The hunters are not quick, and they are very thorough. By evening the hall is empty and every lamp in the house has been put out, one by one, by a young woman with a taper. The tellings differ, but they agree on one thing: that whatever he did, he did it in a great hurry, as if he were afraid there would not be enough time. People remember that he wept. A girl from the village says that she saw him, on the night of the storm, standing on the cliff with his hands over his face.
